rationale: I independently matched the exact proposal, candidate, initial factual-review and live-audit bindings; every one of the 50 additions across 28 boards is an unchanged triple I accepted, with no held or rejected candidate or competing accepted output introduced. Pack, KG and rubric hashes and all nine runtime-source hashes match. I read the extension loader, serving wrapper, generator, audit generator and score/feedback changes, then independently rebuilt the proposal in memory and replayed all 80 served projections; both reproduced the supplied artifacts exactly. Actual node and edge metadata, including provenance, are bound; extensions cannot add concepts, seeds or targets or overwrite core pairs, and mismatching core/graph scopes receive no additions. Original recipes, stored routes and exact minimum par remain intact; the audit checks hidden target IDs and absence of public recipe/route maps. Observed live bounds are at most 24 recipe pairs and 21 projected concepts. Productive openings rise from 190 to 223 and target-ending pairs from 178 to 195; the sport board's three genuine club-class additions change its openings from 4/15 to 7/15 without changing par. Code inspection plus direct score-property checks confirm that unsuccessful attempts do not reduce score, repeated pairs return before counting, extra successful crafts cost 120, hints cost 150 and the floor is 100. Accepted historical/biographic and class relations retain the semantic qualifications in my initial judgments; no new factual inventory is added. This acceptance covers the bounded existing target-round repair only: it does not certify a sandbox, new optional discovery branches, universal successful combinations, independent end-to-end routes for every target, or human enjoyment. Twelve boards still have one productive opening and nineteen still have one target-ending recipe; final recipes should be described as improved coverage with those limitations.
